test_case.title: Cross-email failure then rightful token use
test_case.objective: Verify that a cross-email misuse attempt neither changes an account nor consumes the rightful owner's issued OTP.
preconditions: Users A and B are registered
OTP A is issued for email A

request.auth_profile: NO_JWT_REQUIREMENT_SPECIFIED; use issued email-bound OTP fixtures
request.sequence_or_body_variation: Step 1 sends email B with OTP A and a strong password; step 2 sends email A with the same OTP A

test_data.description: Two-step sequence using disposable users and OTP A
test_data.secret_policy: Use disposable isolated fixtures; no real secrets.

test_case.expected_business_result: Step 1 must not reset either account; step 2 may complete the authoritative owner-bound reset.
test_case.expected_state: After step 1 OTP A remains available for rightful use; after step 2 only A changes and OTP A is invalidated.
test_case.why_ai_missed: The AI tested cross-email binding and valid reset separately but did not execute the recovery sequence proving a failed foreign use does not consume the owner's token.

student_cases.difference_from_ai_generated_suite: Adds a second authoritative owner-use step after the cross-email failure and verifies token state across both requests.
student_cases.why_ai_missed: The AI tested cross-email binding and valid reset separately but did not execute the recovery sequence proving a failed foreign use does not consume the owner's token.

test_case.title: Weak-password failure then strong retry with same OTP
test_case.objective: Verify that a password-policy failure is not treated as successful OTP use and a corrected strong password can use the same issued OTP.
preconditions: A valid email-bound OTP is issued

request.auth_profile: NO_JWT_REQUIREMENT_SPECIFIED; use issued email-bound OTP fixtures
request.sequence_or_body_variation: Step 1 uses a weak password; step 2 retries the same OTP with a strong password

test_data.description: Weak password missing required classes, followed by a compliant password
test_data.secret_policy: Use disposable isolated fixtures; no real secrets.

test_case.expected_business_result: The weak attempt must not complete reset; the strong retry may complete reset with the same still-valid OTP.
test_case.expected_state: Password remains old after step 1; after step 2 it changes and the OTP is invalidated.
test_case.why_ai_missed: The AI stated that a weak-password failure should not consume the token but did not prove recoverability with a follow-up compliant retry.

student_cases.difference_from_ai_generated_suite: Adds an explicit retry transition with the same OTP, making token preservation after business validation failure observable.
student_cases.why_ai_missed: The AI stated that a weak-password failure should not consume the token but did not prove recoverability with a follow-up compliant retry.

test_case.title: Wrong-token failure then correct-token recovery
test_case.objective: Verify that submitting a different six-digit token does not invalidate the actually issued token for the email.
preconditions: A valid OTP is issued for email A

request.auth_profile: NO_JWT_REQUIREMENT_SPECIFIED; use issued email-bound OTP fixtures
request.sequence_or_body_variation: Step 1 submits a different six-digit token; step 2 submits the issued token with a strong password

test_data.description: wrongToken differs from issuedToken while both are six digits
test_data.secret_policy: Use disposable isolated fixtures; no real secrets.

test_case.expected_business_result: The wrong-token request must not reset the password; the issued token remains eligible for its rightful request.
test_case.expected_state: After step 1 password and issued-token state remain unchanged; after step 2 password changes and issued token is invalidated.
test_case.why_ai_missed: The AI covered wrong-token rejection but did not execute the follow-up correct use needed to verify that an attacker guess cannot consume the real token.

student_cases.difference_from_ai_generated_suite: Adds a recovery step using the real token and validates non-consumption after a wrong guess.
student_cases.why_ai_missed: The AI covered wrong-token rejection but did not execute the follow-up correct use needed to verify that an attacker guess cannot consume the real token.

test_case.title: Independent users' OTP invalidation isolation
test_case.objective: Verify that successful use of OTP A invalidates only OTP A and does not invalidate independently issued OTP B.
preconditions: Users A and B each have a valid issued OTP

request.auth_profile: NO_JWT_REQUIREMENT_SPECIFIED; use issued email-bound OTP fixtures
request.sequence_or_body_variation: Reset A successfully, then reset B using OTP B

test_data.secret_policy: Use disposable isolated fixtures; no real secrets.

test_case.expected_business_result: Each user can reset only with their own token; success for A must not revoke B's independent token.
test_case.expected_state: A password changes and OTP A invalidates first; B remains unchanged/valid until its own successful reset, then OTP B invalidates.
test_case.why_ai_missed: The AI checked cross-email misuse and replay but did not cover isolation of two independently valid token lifecycles.

student_cases.difference_from_ai_generated_suite: Uses two simultaneously valid owner-bound tokens and verifies invalidation is scoped to the token used.
student_cases.why_ai_missed: The AI checked cross-email misuse and replay but did not cover isolation of two independently valid token lifecycles.

test_case.title: Replay on user A does not disturb unused token B
test_case.objective: Verify that replaying A's already-used OTP is rejected without consuming or altering B's unused OTP.
preconditions: A and B have valid OTPs
A has completed a successful reset and OTP A is invalidated

request.auth_profile: NO_JWT_REQUIREMENT_SPECIFIED; use issued email-bound OTP fixtures
request.sequence_or_body_variation: Replay OTP A, then use still-unused OTP B for B

test_data.description: Used OTP A and unused OTP B
test_data.secret_policy: Use disposable isolated fixtures; no real secrets.

test_case.expected_business_result: A replay must not create a second reset; B's independent legitimate reset must remain possible.
test_case.expected_state: A remains at its first reset state; B changes only on its own request and OTP B then invalidates.
test_case.why_ai_missed: The AI covered replay for one user but did not combine replay handling with isolation of another user's pending reset state.

student_cases.difference_from_ai_generated_suite: Adds a second user's pending token and proves a replay event cannot cause cross-user lifecycle mutation.
student_cases.why_ai_missed: The AI covered replay for one user but did not combine replay handling with isolation of another user's pending reset state.
